letter:
Subject: Appeal Against Denial of Claim 0b56bd9b-3f60-42be-8338-bca8485e99b0 – Pre‑Existing Disease Waiting Period

Claim Details:  
Claim ID: 0b56bd9b-3f60-42be-8338-bca8485e99b0  
Patient ID: 3893951a-b978-4bd4-bcf1-021e390f0764  
Patient Name: Rahul Sharma  
Date of Claim Submission: 2026-05-27  
Total Claim Amount: INR 22,746.17  
Encounter Class: AMB (Out‑patient)  
Diagnosis: Osteoarthritis of knee (first diagnosed 2026-05-10)  
Procedure: Physical therapy procedure  
Policy: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Plan Code SGH‑SILVER) – Coverage effective 2024-02-27  

Grounds for Appeal:  
The diagnosis of osteoarthritis of the knee was first made on 2026-05-10, which is after the policy start date of 2024-02-27. According to the policy definition, a condition first diagnosed on or after the policy start date is not a Pre‑Existing Disease and therefore the 36‑month PED waiting period does not apply [suraksha_silver_policy#5]. Consequently, the denial based on an unmet pre‑existing disease waiting period is inconsistent with the policy wording [suraksha_silver_policy#11].

Clinical Necessity:  
The treating orthopaedic specialist will attach detailed clinical notes confirming that physical therapy is medically necessary for the management of the patient’s newly diagnosed osteoarthritis of the knee.

Reference to Denial Standards:  
Under the insurer’s own denial standards, the burden of proof lies with the insurer to demonstrate that an exclusion or waiting period is applicable. For a Pre‑Existing Disease denial, the insurer must provide documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed or treated before the policy start date, which has not been supplied in this case [claims_procedure_and_grievance#6].

Specific Request:  
In view of the above, we request that the denial be withdrawn, the claim be re‑processed, and the amount of INR 22,746.17 be paid in full without further delay.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Insurance Desk (on behalf of the treating provider)

### 2.2 Pre-Existing Disease (PED)
Pre-Existing Disease means any condition, ailment, injury or disease that was diagnosed by a physician, or for which medical advice or treatment was received, within 48 months PRIOR TO the first policy start date. citations.section: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Policy Wording) > 4. Waiting Periods > 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
citations.quote:
### 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
Expenses related to a Pre-Existing Disease (as defined in Clause 2.2) are covered only after 36 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date. This waiting period applies ONLY to conditions meeting the definition in Clause 2.2.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C3. Standards for Denial > C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
citations.quote:
### C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
The insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies. For a Pre-Existing Disease denial, the insurer must show documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed or treated before the policy start date.
